newsitem.title: GERMANY: J & H has no comment on Marsh stake talk.
newsitem.headline: J & H has no comment on Marsh stake talk.

text.p: Germany's largest insurance broker Jauch und Huebener declined on Thursday to comment on market talk that Marsh & McLennan was about to take a stake in it.
"We do not comment on rumours," Jauch und Huebener spokesman Peter Hermes told Reuters at a risk management conference in Cologne.
German broking sources at the conference said an announcement was imminent from Jauch & Huebener, with most expecting Marsh & McLennan, the world's largest broker, to take a 49 percent stake.
A spokeswoman for Marsh & McLennan declined immediate comment.
Jauch und Huebener said in April that it was in talks with a number of international broking firms, but declined to identify them.

Industry sources at the time said three names were in the frame as possible partners or buyers -- the two leading UK based brokers -- Sedgwick Group Plc and Willis Corroon Group Plc -- and Marsh & McLennan.
Both Willis and Sedgwick said their policy was not to comment on market rumours.

Jauch & Huebener entered into talks about its future following Marsh & McLennan's acquisition of Johnson & Higgins, which had been at the centre of Unison, an international network of independent insurance brokers.
With the departure of Johnson & Higgins from Unison, the network effectively ceased to exist, forcing the German broker to re-think its global strategy.
